description: SUEWS simulates neighbourhood-scale urban radiation, energy and water balances. The UMEP development group publishes a Fortran physics engine with the SuPy Python interface, tutorials and an input-output reference. Users provide meteorology and the fractions of paved surfaces, buildings, trees, grass, bare soil and water, together with surface and soil parameters. Outputs describe heat, evaporation, interception and soil-water states over the simulated period. Geographic coverage is a configured neighbourhood or local urban area, and time resolution follows its weather inputs. MPL-2.0 source and documentation are freely available. A limitation is that the seven surface classes aggregate diverse real materials and drainage layouts, so local calibration matters. SUEWS can supply urban heat and runoff conditions for building and stormwater resilience studies. The catalogue's model-energyplus treats building energy use at a different scale; no coupling was checked. No sample meteorology or simulation was run.
